extraction_notes.note: One sentence both introduces $\#c(g)$ and states the Möbius-inversion count of exact-symmetry tilings; kept as one definition node since the sentence cannot be split.

Each symmetry-class paragraph identifies $\#c\langle g\rangle$ with a Stanley class/OEIS sequence and quotes a cited product formula; typed as external theorems rather than equations or paper claims, since the formulas are attributed by \cite.

The re-indexing ('inflation') of the cited formulas is the paper's own adjustment; the identification sentences of the $\langle fr\rangle$ paragraph went into the vanishing claim ClP4, while for $\langle r\rangle$ the whole paragraph is TP6.

The two TikZ figures (pairing of triangles along axes) carry only illustration of the parity arguments; captions not made nodes. The intro sentence that product formulas were proven for each symmetry class is background with no specific statement.
The note has no sections and no theorem environments although lemma/theorem/observation are declared; every node is prose, so section fields are empty.

nodes.statement: If we denote the number of tilings which have at least the symmetries of g le langle f, rrangle by \#c(g) then the number of tilings having exactly the symmetries of g is given by the M\"obius function of the incidence algebra of this poset: sum_h le langle f, rrangle mu(g, h) \#c(h).
nodes.raw_latex: If we denote the number of tilings which have at least the symmetries of $g \le \langle f, r\rangle$ by $\#c(g)$ then the number of tilings having exactly the symmetries of $g$ is given by the M\"obius function of the incidence algebra of this poset: $\sum_{h \le \langle f, r\rangle} \mu(g, h) \#c(h)$.

conclusions: \#clangle erangle is the most studied of the cases, being simply the number of tilings (Stanley's case 1).
It is A008793 in OEIS, and has formula \#clangle erangle(n) = prod_i=0^n-1 fraci!(i+2n)!(i+n)!^2 .

nodes.statement: \#clangle frrangle is A181119, ``transpose-complementary plane partitions'' (Stanley's case 6), but there's a slight catch. It is non-zero only for even n; there is a simple geometric explanation. The axis of symmetry bisects 2n triangles, which must pair up along the axis because otherwise they would be forced to pair with two triangles to maintain the symmetry. But the pairs start at the centre of the hexagon, so if n is odd there are two triangles on opposite edges which can't be paired. (See figure 1). The upshot is that the given formula must be inflated as \#clangle frrangle(2m) = binom3m-1m prod_i=0^2m-3 frac(i+4m)!(2i+2)!(2i+2m+2)!(i+2m)! .
conclusions: \#clangle frrangle is A181119, ``transpose-complementary plane partitions'' (Stanley's case 6), but there's a slight catch.

nodes.raw_latex: $\#c\langle fr\rangle$ is A181119, ``transpose-complementary plane partitions'' (Stanley's case 6), but there's a slight catch. It is non-zero only for even $n$; there is a simple geometric explanation. The axis of symmetry bisects $2n$ triangles, which must pair up along the axis because otherwise they would be forced to pair with two triangles to maintain the symmetry. But the pairs start at the centre of the hexagon, so if $n$ is odd there are two triangles on opposite edges which can't be paired. (See figure 1). The upshot is that the given formula must be inflated as $\#c\langle fr\rangle(2m) = \binom{3m-1}{m} \prod_{i=0}^{2m-3} \frac{(i+4m)!(2i+2)!}{(2i+2m+2)!(i+2m)!}$ \cite{Proctor88}.

But the pairs start at the centre of the hexagon, so if n is odd there are two triangles on opposite edges which can't be paired. (See figure 1). The upshot is that the given formula must be inflated as \#clangle frrangle(2m) = binom3m-1m prod_i=0^2m-3 frac(i+4m)!(2i+2)!(2i+2m+2)!(i+2m)! .

nodes.statement: \#clangle rrangle is A049503, which is cryptically described as ``A005130^2'' and ``Expansion of generating function A_QT^(1)(4n)''. It corresponds to the cyclically symmetric and self-complementary plane partitions (Stanley's case 9). Note that again we must inflate the sequence (since langle r^3rangle le langle rrangle the same argument applies), and when we do so we get that \#clangle rrangle(2m) = prod_i=0^m-1 frac(3i+1)!^2(i+m)!^2 .
conclusions: \#clangle rrangle is A049503, which is cryptically described as ``A005130^2'' and ``Expansion of generating function A_QT^(1)(4n)''.
It corresponds to the cyclically symmetric and self-complementary plane partitions (Stanley's case 9).

nodes.raw_latex: $\#c\langle r\rangle$ is A049503, which is cryptically described as ``A005130$^2$'' and ``Expansion of generating function $A_{QT}^{(1)}(4n)$''. It corresponds to the cyclically symmetric and self-complementary plane partitions (Stanley's case 9). Note that again we must inflate the sequence (since $\langle r^3\rangle \le \langle r\rangle$ the same argument applies), and when we do so we get that $\#c\langle r\rangle(2m) = \prod_{i=0}^{m-1} \frac{(3i+1)!^2}{(i+m)!^2}$ \cite{Kuperberg94}.
